The manufacturer must document a system to assign unique device identification in accordance with part 830 of this chapter, document procedures for traceability in accordance with part 821 of this chapter, and notify the FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter. Advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with part 806 of this chapter. The requirements apply to devices that are automated with computer software, devices listed in table 1, devices that support or sustain life, and enforcement of compliance. If applicable, the requirements apply to class II, class III, and class I devices listed in paragraph (c)(1) of this section and table 1 to paragraph (c)(2) of this section. The devices that support or sustain life must comply with the requirements in Traceability for Implantable Devices, Clause 7.5.9.2 in ISO 13485, in addition to all other applicable requirements in this part, as appropriate. The enforcement of compliance renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. [4][5]

Part 821 is a regulation under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (the act) that implements section 519(e) of the act. A distributor, final distributor, or multiple distributor of any tracked device shall, upon purchasing or otherwise acquiring any interest in such a device, promptly provide the manufacturer tracking the device with the information. The following definitions and terms apply to this part: the following definitions and terms apply to this part: [1]. The importer of a tracked device shall be considered the manufacturer and shall be required to comply with all requirements of this part applicable to manufacturers. Importers must keep all information required under this part in the United States. [7]. The useful life of a device is the time a device is in use or in distribution for use. For example, a record may be retired if the person maintaining the record becomes aware of the fact that the device is no longer in use, has been explanted, returned to the manufacturer, or the patient has died. [8]. Persons required to maintain records under this part shall maintain such records for the useful life of each tracked device they manufacture or distribute. [10].

raw_model_output:
21 CFR Part 11 covers the requirements for electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records. It sets forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper. The regulations in this part set forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper.

- 21 CFR 11.100(a): Each electronic signature shall be unique to one individual and shall not be reused by, or reassigned to, anyone else.
- 21 CFR 11.10: Persons who use closed systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ procedures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, when appropriate, the confidentiality of electronic records, and to ensure that the signer cannot readily repudiate the signed record as not genuine.
- 21 CFR 11.1(a): The regulations in this part set forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper.
- 21 CFR 11.200(a): Electronic signatures that are not based upon biometrics shall not be used in the same way as biometric signatures.
- 21 CFR 11.2(a): For records required to be maintained but not submitted to the agency, persons may use electronic records in lieu of paper records or electronic signatures in lieu of traditional signatures, in whole or in part, provided that the requirements of this part are met.
- 21 CFR 11.300: Persons who use electronic signatures based upon use of identification codes in combination with passwords shall employ controls to ensure their security and integrity. Such controls shall include:
- 21 CFR 11.30: Persons who use open systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ procedures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, as appropriate, the confidentiality of electronic records from the point of their creation to the point of their receipt. Such procedures and controls shall include those identified in § 11.10, as appropriate, and additional measures such as document encryption and use of appropriate digital signature standards to ensure, as necessary under the circumstances, record authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality.
- 21 CFR 11.3(a): The definitions and interpretations of terms contained in section 201 of the act apply to those terms when used in this part.

It sets forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper. The regulations in this part set forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper.

- 21 CFR 11.100(a): Each electronic signature shall be unique to one individual and shall not be reused by, or reassigned to, anyone else.
- 21 CFR 11.10: Persons who use closed systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ procedures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, when appropriate, the confidentiality of electronic records, and to ensure that the signer cannot readily repudiate the signed record as not genuine.
- 21 CFR 11.1(a): The regulations in this part set forth the criteria under which the agency considers electronic records, electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records to be trustworthy, reliable, and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures executed on paper.
- 21 CFR 11.200(a): Electronic signatures that are not based upon biometrics shall not be used in the same way as biometric signatures.
- 21 CFR 11.2(a): For records required to be maintained but not submitted to the agency, persons may use electronic records in lieu of paper records or electronic signatures in lieu of traditional signatures, in whole or in part, provided that the requirements of this part are met.
- 21 CFR 11.300: Persons who use electronic signatures based upon use of identification codes in combination with passwords shall employ controls to ensure their security and integrity. Such controls shall include:
- 21 CFR 11.30: Persons who use open systems to create, modify, maintain, or transmit electronic records shall employ procedures and controls designed to ensure the authenticity, integrity, and, as appropriate, the confidentiality of electronic records from the point of their creation to the point of their receipt. Such procedures and controls shall include those identified in § 11.10, as appropriate, and additional measures such as document encryption and use of appropriate digital signature standards to ensure, as necessary under the circumstances, record authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality.
- 21 CFR 11.3(a): The definitions and interpretations of terms contained in section 201 of the act apply to those terms when used in this part.

raw_model_output:
Who is subject to the dietary supplement CGMP requirements of 21 CFR Part 111? [1]  

The requirements under this subpart F for written procedures apply to the responsibilities of the quality control operations, including written procedures for conducting a material review and making a disposition decision, and for approving or rejecting any reprocessing. [1]  

Quality control personnel must ensure that your manufacturing, packaging, labeling, and holding operations ensure the quality of the dietary supplement and that the dietary supplement is packaged and labeled as specified in the master manufacturing record. [1]  

You must have qualified employees who manufacture, package, label, or hold dietary supplements. [1]  

Quality control operations for returned dietary supplements must include reviewing and approving decisions about whether to investigate a product complaint and reviewing and approving the findings and followup action of any investigation performed. [1]  

Quality control operations for product complaints must include reviewing and approving decisions about whether to investigate a product complaint and reviewing and approving the findings and followup action of any investigation performed. [1]  

You must assign qualified personnel to supervise the manufacturing, packaging, labeling, or holding of dietary supplements. [1]  

You must make and keep the records required under this subpart F in accordance with subpart P of this part. [1]  

You must make and keep records required under this subpart B in accordance with subpart P of this part. [1]  

You must establish and follow written procedures for fulfilling the requirements of this subpart G. [1]  

You must visually examine each immediate container or grouping of immediate containers in a shipment for appropriate content label, container damage, or broken seals to determine whether the container condition may have resulted in contamination or deterioration of the components. [1]  

You must keep the grounds of your physical plant in a condition that protects against the contamination of components, dietary supplements, or contact surfaces. [1]  

You must visually examine each immediate container or grouping of immediate containers in a shipment for appropriate content label, container damage, or broken seals to determine whether the container condition may have resulted in contamination or deterioration of the packaging and labels. [1]

raw_model_output: Under Part 111, the responsibilities of quality control personnel include ensuring the quality of dietary supplements through written procedures for conducting material reviews, making disposition decisions, and approving or rejecting reprocessing. Quality control personnel must also ensure the quality of the dietary supplement and packaging, labeling, and holding operations, including performing operations that involve material reviews and disposition decisions. They must prevent microbial contamination by excluding sick or infected personnel and implementing hygienic practices. Quality control operations for laboratory operations associated with the production and process control system must include material reviews and disposition decisions. Quality control operations for components, packaging, and labels before use in the manufacture of a dietary supplement must include these responsibilities. Quality control personnel must ensure the quality of the master manufacturing record, batch production record, and manufacturing operations. They must also make and keep records required under this subpart F in accordance with subpart P of this part. Under this subpart F, quality control personnel must ensure the quality of dietary supplements through written procedures for fulfilling the requirements of this subpart F. They must visually examine each immediate container or grouping of immediate containers in a shipment for appropriate content label, container damage, or broken seals to determine whether the container condition may have resulted in contamination or deterioration of the components. Grounds must be maintained in a condition that protects against contamination of components, dietary supplements, or contact surfaces. The methods for adequate ground maintenance include visual examination of the grounds. You must assign qualified personnel to supervise the manufacturing, packaging, labeling, or holding of dietary supplements. Under this subpart F, you must make and keep records required under this subpart F in accordance with subpart P of this part. Under this subpart B, you must make and keep records required under this subpart B in accordance with subpart P of this part. Grounds must be maintained in a condition that protects against contamination of components, dietary supplements, or contact surfaces. The methods for adequate ground maintenance include visual examination of the grounds. You must assign qualified personnel to supervise the manufacturing, packaging, labeling, or holding of dietary supplements. Under this subpart F, you must make and keep records required under this subpart F in accordance with subpart P of this part. Under this subpart B, you must make and keep records required under this subpart B in accordance with subpart P of this part. If a manufacturer engages in only some operations subject to the requirements in this part, it must comply with those applicable to the operations in which it is engaged.
